initialize_result.instructions:
WhatJobs finds live job listings and reports on pay and hiring from them.

How the inputs work across these tools:
- One request that names several roles or places is one search: put the first role and place in keyword and location, and the others in more_keywords and more_locations. Every role is searched in every place, and the results come back together in one view.
- When the places are in different countries, leave market empty so each place uses its own country.
- A salary comparison takes all its roles and places in one call, through keywords and locations.
- For more results from the same search, repeat it with the same inputs and the next chunk_number.

tools.description:
Search live WhatJobs job listings by role and place.

Use this when the user wants to find jobs, vacancies, internships or other work, or asks to see more results from a job search.

Inputs:
- keyword: the role, job function, skill or industry only. Leave out the place and filler words such as jobs, vacancies, roles, hiring, in, near, around, at or within.
- location: the place to search (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask for jobs near them. For remote work use "Remote", alone or with a place such as "California remote"; only listings that say they are remote come back.
- market: optional country code; if empty it is inferred from location. Supported values: uk (United Kingdom), us (United States), ca (Canada), de (Germany), in (India), pk (Pakistan), br (Brazil), es (Spain), ae (United Arab Emirates), mx (Mexico), ar (Argentina), za (South Africa), at (Austria), au (Australia), be (Belgium), bh (Bahrain), cl (Chile), co (Colombia), cr (Costa Rica), ch (Switzerland), do (Dominican Republic), dz (Algeria), ng (Nigeria), nl (Netherlands), fr (France), dk (Denmark), eg (Egypt), id (Indonesia), my (Malaysia), om (Oman), ph (Philippines), qa (Qatar), sa (Saudi Arabia), sg (Singapore), tz (Tanzania), ug (Uganda), fi (Finland), gr (Greece), gt (Guatemala), hk (Hong Kong), ie (Ireland), it (Italy), kw (Kuwait), lt (Lithuania), lu (Luxembourg), ma (Morocco), no (Norway), nz (New Zealand), pa (Panama), pe (Peru), pl (Poland), pr (Puerto Rico), pt (Portugal), ru (Russia), se (Sweden), th (Thailand), tr (Turkey), ve (Venezuela), bd (Bangladesh), bo (Bolivia), cn (China), cz (Czech Republic), gh (Ghana), ke (Kenya), hu (Hungary), jp (Japan), kr (South Korea), lk (Sri Lanka), mg (Madagascar), py (Paraguay), ro (Romania), sn (Senegal), sv (El Salvador), tn (Tunisia), ua (Ukraine), uy (Uruguay), vn (Vietnam).
- chunk_number: the result batch. Use 1 for a new search and add 1 each time the user asks for more.
- more_keywords: optional. Other roles to search in the same call when the user asks about several.
- more_locations: optional. Other places to search in the same call when the user asks about several.

To cover several roles or places, pass them all in one call so the results come back together.

Examples:
- sales in Bracknell -> keyword="sales", location="Bracknell", market="uk"
- software engineer jobs near Manchester -> keyword="software engineer", location="Manchester", market="uk"
- nurse jobs in Berlin -> keyword="nurse", location="Berlin", market="de"
- comptable à Paris -> keyword="comptable", location="Paris", market="fr"
- accountant jobs in Dubai -> keyword="accountant", location="Dubai, United Arab Emirates", market="ae"
- developer jobs in Singapore -> keyword="developer", location="Singapore", market="sg"
- nurse or carer jobs in Leeds and York -> keyword="nurse", location="Leeds", more_keywords=["carer"], more_locations=["York"], market="uk"

Returns up to 10 listings per batch (up to 20 across several roles or places), each with title, company, location, salary when the listing states one, posted date, summary and apply link, plus paging details. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.

tools.description:
Show what a job pays, from the salaries in current WhatJobs listings: typical range, median, lowest and highest, plus a few listings with salaries.

Use this when the user asks how much a role pays or earns, salary ranges, or whether a salary is good, e.g. "How much does a nurse earn in Paris?" or "Data analyst salary in London".

Inputs:
- keyword: the job role only (e.g. "nurse", "software engineer").
- location: the place to search (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask for jobs near them. May be empty for the whole country.
- market: optional country code; if empty it is inferred from location. Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

Figures are in the country's own currency, for the pay period most listings use (per year in most countries, per month in some); the result says which. The result includes a link to all matching jobs on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.

tools.description:
Compare what a job pays across places, or what different jobs pay in one place, from the salaries in current WhatJobs listings: the typical range and median for each, side by side.

Use this when the user wants pay compared, e.g. "Nurse salary in London vs Manchester", "Do developers earn more in Berlin or Munich?", "Which pays more in Toronto, accountant or bookkeeper?".

Inputs:
- keywords: one or more job roles only (e.g. ["nurse"], or ["accountant", "bookkeeper"]).
- locations: one or more places to compare (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask about jobs near them.
- market: optional. Leave empty to let each location use its own country (so "Paris" and "Berlin" compare France and Germany). Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

Up to 4 role x place combinations are compared. Each row is in that country's own currency (amounts are not converted between currencies) and says its pay period (per year in most countries). Each row links to that search on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.

If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.

tools.description:

Use this when the user asks where the most jobs are, how much demand there is, or to compare cities or roles, e.g. "Where are the most data analyst jobs in Germany?", "More jobs for nurses or carers in Leeds?", "Paris vs Berlin for developers".

tools.description:
Show only recently posted WhatJobs listings for a role and place, newest first.

Use this when the user asks for new, fresh, recent or today's jobs, e.g. "Any electrician jobs posted today in Manchester?" or "New marketing jobs this week in Madrid".

Inputs:
- keyword: the job role only.
- location: the place to search (city, region or country), not the user's own location unless they ask for jobs near them.
- posted_within_days: 1 for today/yesterday, 7 for this week (default), up to 30.
- For remote work, put "Remote" in location, alone or with a place; only listings that say they are remote come back.
- more_keywords: optional. Other roles to search in the same call when the user asks about several.
- more_locations: optional. Other places to search in the same call when the user asks about several.
- market: optional country code; if empty it is inferred from location. Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

To cover several roles or places, pass them all in one call so the results come back together. The result includes a link to all matching jobs on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.

tools.description:
Find WhatJobs listings that fit a person's background: searches up to 4 target job titles at once and ranks the jobs by how well the title matches and how many of their skills each listing mentions.

Use this when the user shares their CV, experience or skills and asks what jobs suit them, e.g. "Here's my CV, what should I apply for in Manchester?".

Inputs:
- job_titles: 1-4 job titles that fit the person (you choose them from what they shared).
- skills: up to 10 key skills or tools (e.g. "Python", "SQL", "forklift licence").
- location: where they want to work (the place to search). For remote work use "Remote", alone or with a place.
- market: optional country code; if empty it is inferred from location. Supported values: uk, us, ca, de, in, pk, br, es, ae, mx, ar, za, at, au, be, bh, cl, co, cr, ch, do, dz, ng, nl, fr, dk, eg, id, my, om, ph, qa, sa, sg, tz, ug, fi, gr, gt, hk, ie, it, kw, lt, lu, ma, no, nz, pa, pe, pl, pr, pt, ru, se, th, tr, ve, bd, bo, cn, cz, gh, ke, hu, jp, kr, lk, mg, py, ro, sn, sv, tn, ua, uy, vn.

Pass only titles and skills. Never pass CV text, names, contact details or other personal data. The result includes a link to all matching jobs on WhatJobs. Results come only from WhatJobs. Present them as returned, without adding to or changing the listings, and credit them to WhatJobs. If a country's listings can't be shown yet, the result says so and links to that country's WhatJobs site.
